Welcome
Dear Families,
It is my greatest pleasure to welcome you to Shrewton CE Primary School.
We are a small school set in the heart of the village where we are passionately committed to giving our pupils an engaging and memorable learning experience that creates a love of learning for the rest of their lives. We pride ourselves on our inclusive, topic based approach which sees all pupils be successful learners and consequently our school go from strength to strength.
Built on a strong set of Christian Values, our overarching value of love is at the very core of our school. We are pleased to promote a loving learning community in which all pupils and members of our community can believe, achieve and grow, as noted in our last Church of England SIAMs Inspection for which we were judged to be 'good'. (Feb 2020)
I hope that within the pages of our website you get a flavour of our school and everything we have to offer. If you would like to come and see us in action, it would be my pleasure to give you a tour personally, call 01980 620362 or email enquiries@shrewton.dsat.org.uk to make an appointment or alternatively with any queries that you may have.
Mrs Anna Howell (Headteacher)

pageCache.pageTitle: Shrewton CE Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
How do we promote British Values at Shrewton?
British values are inherent in all aspects of academy life at Shrewton Academy. As a diverse community, we celebrate these values, to enable our children to be global citizens of the future.
These are the British Values we promote at Shrewton Academy:
We reflect British values in all aspects of school life. We promote these values in the ways in which staff model behaviour during lessons, whilst moving around the school and during play and lunch times. These values are particularly focused on during Personal, Social, Health Education (PSHE) lessons and whole school Acts of Worship and assemblies.
Democracy
Tolerance
The Rule of Law
Individual Liberty
Equality
Respect
Democracy
At Shrewton children have many opportunities for their voices to be heard. We have a school council which meets regularly to discuss issues raised by their peers. Two school council members for each year group from years 2 -6 are voted for by their class. Pupil voice is heard regularly through surveys throughout the year. This allows pupils to put forward their views about the school. Democracy is explored through a series of lessons in our PSHE curriculum.
The Rule of Law
Pupils are taught why we have laws; that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. The importance of rules are taught when dealing with behaviour and through school acts of worship.
Individual Liberty
Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms. They are encouraged to make choices in a safe and supportive environment and advised how to exercise their rights safely, for example through our E-Safety and PSHE lessons.
Children learn that with rights come responsibilities. They learn that their actions affect their own rights and those of others. As active learners, children are taught to reflect on their own responsibilities in school. Children are given the opportunity to reflect on the issues through dedicated classroom reflection time where they can also contribute to the class reflection book.
Respect
Respect is one of our school values. Children are taught that respect is mutual and must be earned. We listen to pupils’ and parents’ views through the use of pupil surveys and through the annual questionnaire to parents. All members of the school community treat each other respectfully. Through acts of worship and a weekly PHSE lesson, children learn about their world, different beliefs and inspiring people in order to help develop their respect.
Tolerance
At Shrewton, we embrace cultural diversity in our school and the wider community. Children are encouraged to reflect on their own identity and culture. As a Church school, we focus on Christian values but teach the children about a range of religions and cultures across the world to promote understanding.
As a Primary School within the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust, we seek to promote these values through the Trust vision statement. Our curriculum approach ensures that these values are addressed frequently through Religious Education, personal and social development, behaviour and reward systems and circle time, as well as through Collective Worship and extra-curricular activities.
As an organisation, we will actively challenge pupils, staff and parents who express opinions contrary to the above values. All of our staff have undertaken PREVENT training so are alert to the need to respond to potential extremism and radicalisation.

Vision and Values
Our Values shape us as learners and as people
‘Believe, Achieve, Grow’
Our vision and values are at the core of all we do. They underpin our teaching, learning and daily relationships and provide a firm foundation for all aspects of our children’s development. Our aim is to provide a happy and caring learning community where every child is known and feels special. We are rightly proud of our pupils, their care for each other and their achievements.
We uphold core Christian values which provide the focus for collective worship, class worship, quiet reflection and relationship development.
Love is patient, love is kind.
It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
It is not rude, it is not self-seeking,
it is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrongs.
Love does not delight in evil but rejoices with the truth.
It always protects, always trusts, always hopes, always perseveres.
Love is the overarching value for our school. It is the foundational message of Christian teaching and summarises of all our six core Christian values:

Wraparound Care
Breakfast & After School Clubs
Breakfast Club will run every morning from 7.30am to 8.45am when the children will be escorted to class.
The After School Club will run from 3.15pm to 5.15pm on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday and 3.15pm - 4.30pm on Friday.
The clubs will be run by the school and will therefore comply with school policies and procedures. The club will only be open to pupils registered at the school.
All sessions will need to be pre-booked and paid for in advance via the Arbor app. Bookings must be received by 9am on a Monday morning for the following week's sessions. There is no requirement to book your child in every day (or every week), but you will need to book in advance.
Breakfast will be offered to the children. A light snack and a drink will be offered in the after school club.
The club will operate a range of activities over the course of the week including games, sports, craft and seasonal activities.

Governance
Letter from the Chair of Governors
Welcome to Shrewton Primary School.
We hope this website gives you a feeling for our school, and our shared vision for a place where all children grow to believe in themselves and their abilities – as they build the skills, knowledge, and experiences they will need on their life journeys.
The children at Shrewton have a happy and caring environment in which to learn, build friendships and be adventurous. We aim to help our children to be confident, sensitive to others, interested in the world around them, and prepared for all the opportunities and challenges life has to offer.
Our school is a community driven by love. This extends through the school’s leadership, staff, pupils, parents, the Church and the broader community. By coming together we can all help children build the best possible foundations for their futures.
The school’s governors (or Academy Standards and Ethos Committee) are a team of volunteers from different walks of life. We bring a range of skills and experiences to help support and challenge the school as part of the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust (DSAT) governance structure. By working closely with DSAT and the staff team, we help to provide the strategic direction for the school, to make sure the schools’ performance is evaluated and continuously improves, and to ensure the school’s legal obligations are met and that the school keeps abreast with new initiatives. At the same time we help to keep the school true to its vision, with the lives and learning of our children at its heart.
If you would like to hear more about our school or the work of the school’s governors please visit the school or contact me via the school office.
With thanks and best wishes,
DSAT Scheme of Delegation We are members of the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust and the governance of the Trust belongs to the main DSAT Board. Our Scheme of Delegation also includes our Constitution and Terms of Reference. Paper copies can be obtained through the school office or by using the contact us option on this website. You can find details of the Trust Board and details of our Trust Governance by visiting the trustees page,
The chair of Governors is Mrs Fiona Whitworth can be contacted via the school office or by email chair@shrewton.dsat.org.uk
The clerk to the governing body is Sarah Nash who can be contacted by email snash@dsat.org.uk

Curriculum
Our Curriculum Pledge (Intent)
At Shrewton CE Primary School we aim to deliver an accessible curriculum that equips all ages and abilities for the future through creative and inspiring, knowledge-based learning opportunities within a safe, inclusive and nurturing environment with love at its core.
We employ the follow strategies to best deliver our curriculum:
An inclusive learning environment,
Collaborative learning opportunities,
Peer mentoring,
A broad curriculum offer,
Additional creative curriculum knowledge days,
Inspiring staff in a stimulating environment.
Curriculum Drivers – what drives our curriculum?
The National Curriculum sets the expectation of what children should be taught as part of their academic learning. However, we want more for our children. They deserve to experience and learn about all that life has to offer. We have high expectations for our pupils learning journey and with this in mind, as a staff, we agreed on four main drivers that underpin our curriculum to ensure it is enriched, personalised and aspirational.
Our Curriculum Implementation
We are fully committed to giving our children a memorable learning journey from Early Years to Year 6 that promotes and develops a love of life-long learning. Therefore, we make the following pledge of non-negotiable enrichment experiences that focus on developing the whole child throughout their time at our school.
Our flight path is inclusive of some of the destinations your child may travel to through their time at Shrewton. These destinations may change but the goal is for us to explore both our local and wider community, creating memorable experiences for all.
